$comment: Which scenarios each eval_flagship.yml tier runs on the Strix Halo pool. Lanes
(eval/ci_lanes.json) say how categories are grouped for the full sweep; this file
says which scenarios a smaller tier runs and on how many machines.
smoke   - every RC tag. 30 stable scenarios, 13 of them protected, on 3 machines.
full    - an RC nominated for promotion ([full eval] in its tag message, or a
dispatch with tier=full). Every lane, minus the scenarios below marked
leaves_full.
backlog - weekly (Sunday 06:17 UTC). Scenarios that always or almost always fail
and are not protected (leaves_full: true), plus the noisiest ones, which
also stay in the full sweep. Its trend artifact tracks the road to 80%.
Picked from 16 runs of the flagship eval, 2026-10-06..21 (#5493,
eval/analysis/flagship_scenarios_2026-10.csv on that PR). A smoke scenario passed
at least 90% of at least 10 runs and never timed out, so one FAIL means something.
gemma_halo_minutes is that data's median, so a guide for packing, not a promise:
the pool now scores Qwen3.6, whose times come from the first tier runs.
PROTECTED scenarios never leave the full sweep: every scenario in gaia_honesty,
adversarial, error_recovery and gaia_resilience, every one tagged security, and
every one with 'injection' in its id. util/eval_tiers.py check (run by
tests/unit/eval/test_eval_tiers.py and by the lanes job) enforces that, the
machine limits, and that smoke + full + backlog together cover every scenario.
A machine may not mix gaia_* categories with others: they need fixtures and
auto-approval the others must not run with. memory may share a machine with other
non-gaia categories; it alone gets the live store (EVAL_MEMORY_CATEGORIES).
